name: OPA128
type: Difet electrometer-grade op-amp, single, TO-99 can
tagline: Burr-Brown's 75 fA electrometer can, collected by Chinese DIYers for preamps despite only 1 MHz GBW.

lineage.note: Difet process. Datasheet PDS-653, last printing rev E (1995-05). Improved pin-for-pin AD515 replacement.
Re-issued datasheet as SBOS148. Went NRND, then discontinued; OPA128JM last-time buy 2020-05-14.
OPA128 datasheet calls itself an improved pin-for-pin replacement for the AD515.
OPA129: related Difet electrometer amp in SO-8; TI E2E thread covers the differences.

part_numbers.note: Base part. Grades JM/KM/LM/SM, all TO-99; TI NRND, then lifetime buy.
Lowest commercial grade. DigiKey last-time buy 2020-05-14.
Mid commercial grade. Listed NRND/discontinued; presumably obsolete after 2020 LTB.
Presumed best grade (75 fA max), unconfirmed. Presumably obsolete after 2020 LTB.
Military-temperature grade. Pulled cans sold as 'OPA128SM/883'; /883B code unconfirmed.

key_specs.condition: Aol 110 dB min, CMRR 90 dB min

reputation.summary: Niche, mostly Chinese audio praise. A CSDN listening ranking puts 'OPA128SM x2' just below the OPA1612 for overtones and resolution. CN DIYers collect military-pulled OPA128SM/883 gold cans as '发烧运放' for preamps, often beside the OPA627. Low GBW and slew make it a poor general-purpose audio part, though some like it for DAC I/V. It was designed as an electrometer.
typical_uses: Preamp line stage with TO-99 adapter (CN DIY)
caveats: Only 1 MHz GBW and 3 V/µs slew; not a general-purpose audio op-amp.
Single channel in TO-99: dual-socket use needs two cans and an adapter.
Discontinued (TI LTB 2020); most stock is pulled or surplus.
Praise comes from a small number of Chinese enthusiast sources.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA128-specific fake reports. Discontinued since 2020; CN stock is sold as pulled 'OPA128SM/883' cans, so distrust 'new' stock. Remarking is plausible. fA bias needs an electrometer setup to confirm; supply current, GBW and slew are quicker checks.

open_questions: Dates and content of PDS-653 revisions A–D; does the 1989 Burr-Brown data book hold one?
Did TI ever issue SBOS148A after the September 2000 release?
Per-grade (JM/KM/LM/SM) limits for bias current, offset and drift.
Voltage and current noise density figures.
Did a separate OPA128SM/883B ordering code exist? Is the die unchanged through the TI era?

claims_confirmed: Datasheet copy is Burr-Brown PDS-653E, May 1995 (https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/opa128-445402.pdf).
75 fA max bias, 500 µV max offset, 5 µV/°C drift, 110 dB min Aol, 90 dB min CMRR; improved AD515 replacement (https://www.alldatasheet.com/html-pdf/56727/BURR-BROWN/OPA128/500/1/OPA128.html).
OPA128JM end of life, last-time buy 2020-05-14 (https://www.digikey.com/product-detail/en/texas-instruments/OPA128JM/OPA128JM-ND/301117).
OPA129 is a related part, compared on TI E2E (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/712204/opa129-differences-from-opa128).
PDS-653E copies read '©1986 Burr-Brown Corporation PDS-653E Printed in U.S.A. May, 1995' (https://www.electro-tech-online.com/custompdfs/2011/03/opa128.pdf).
TI-hosted OPA128 copy: 11 pages, file published Sep 27, 2000 (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=83971).

OPA128 indexed at page 1-73 of Burr-Brown's 1988 Data Book Supplement, dated July 1987 (https://ftp.mirrorservice.org/sites/www.bitsavers.org/components/burrBrown/_dataBooks/1988_Burr-Brown_Integrated_Circuits_Data_Book_Supplement.pdf).
